newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GOULD JOB NOT ON THE LINE, SAYS WELSH OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GOULD JOB NOT ON THE LINE, SAYS WELSH OFFICIAL.

text.p: Wales manager Bobby Gould's job was not on the line following alleged racist remarks he made to striker Nathan Blake, a senior official said.
The Football Association of Wales management committee was due to discuss the issue at a special meeting later on Tuesday.
But FAW president Brian Dear stressed that Gould's job was "not the issue.
"We're simply going to investigate and report to the full council over what went on and who said what. That's what this is all about, not Bobby's job,'' said Fear on Tuesday.
Gould denied he was a racist and apologised to Blake for "any misunderstanding" over his remarks made in training before a World Cup qualifier against Belgium last month.
Fear described the incident as a storm in a teacup and said that Blake's acceptance of a Gould apology had taken the heat out of the situation.
Gould's contract as Wales manager ends in December but Fear hinted that it would be extended.
"Two years is not enough to build a team," he said. "I think he should be given another contract to see us through the European championships.''
Since Gould took over as Welsh boss at the start of the 1995-6 season, two wins over San Marino and another against Moldova have been his only successes in 12 internationals.
